subject: Unexpectedly bad results with Poisson time series

messages.author: 26c06a219175f2cf
messages.subject: Unexpectedly bad results with Poisson time series
parts:
Hi,

I am testing INLA with simple Poisson time series models, and got some surprising results. As a latent states x, I simulated Gaussian AR(1) process and generated my observations as a Poisson(exp(x)). The autoregressive parameter tends to estimate fine, but sigma/tau is way off. I'll attach a document which illustrates the issue and compares the results with Stan.

I have tried to check the prior definitions etc but I can't see any problems in the model specifications. I know that binomial models with small counts can be problematic with INLA but is this common phenomenon in Poisson models as well, or am I doing something wrong?

Best regards,

Jouni

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Unexpectedly bad results with Poisson time series
parts:
Hi,
Check your parameterisations.
The precision parameter for ar1 in inla is the marginal precision (called kappa in http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/doc/latent/ar1.pdf ), but your arima.sim() call specified the stad.dev. of the AR process innovation terms.

Finn

yes, this is almost surely the case. for small length, there might also
be a difference in the 'initial conditions' as INLA computes the exact
marginals for (x_1...,x_p) for the AR(p), whereas many packages do not
do this (I'm unsure about what R does here though...)
